items.title: ₹10,000 a month for 10 years in flexi cap funds
items.text: A ₹10,000 monthly SIP started in November 2016 in the middle-ranked of the 19 flexi cap funds with a 10-year record (Regular plans) is worth about ₹23.0 lakh today, on ₹12.0 lakh put in: about 13% a year. That decade included the 2020 crash. The weakest fund's SIP is at ₹20.2 lakh and the strongest at ₹31.3 lakh.

items.title: Small Cap: SIPs started at the Nov 2025 high are back in profit
items.text: In 30 of 31 small cap funds (Regular plans), a monthly SIP started in November 2025, when the Nifty 50 last peaked, is already worth more than the money put in, although the Nifty 50 itself is still below that high. The median SIP is +5.0%. Instalments made while prices were lower bought more units, which is how an SIP recovers before the market does.

items.title: Regular or Direct: what the extra cost pays for
items.text: A fund's Regular plan typically costs 0.98% a year more than its Direct plan. That difference pays a distributor, like us, to help choose and combine funds, rebalance, plan tax, handle the paperwork and keep you on plan when markets fall. If you would rather do all of that yourself, the Direct plan of the same fund costs less: on a ₹10,000 monthly SIP for 20 years at an assumed 12%, the gap adds up to about ₹10.2 lakh.

items.title: Where active funds beat their index
items.text: Over the last 3 years, 13 of 23 multi cap funds (Regular plans) beat their index (TRI), the highest share among the main categories. It varies a lot: in large cap it was 8 of 30, so which fund you hold matters as much as which category.
